reviewNotice: Recorded usage only: the control had one TLS transport failure whose billing is unknown. Its 66 successful responses match Codex’s final usage totals. Complete-session cost and savings remain unverified. Both patches met all five criteria.

criteria.behavior: A custom Prefetch queryset for a forward ForeignKey with no explicit database uses the parent instance’s database through the existing router, including correct related data when default and other contain different rows.
The same parent-database behavior holds for a reverse OneToOneField custom Prefetch queryset with no explicit database.
An explicit database selected on the custom queryset with using() continues to take precedence; the fix does not force all custom querysets onto the parent database.
Existing router behavior and instance hints are preserved, with routing performed at the appropriate point rather than prematurely fixing the default database.

Existing queryset reuse, cached-relation handling, empty-prefetch behavior and unaffected many-to-many paths retain their observable behavior; the patch does not bypass prefetching or add unnecessary per-object database queries.

verdicts.evidence: ForwardManyToOneDescriptor now calls `queryset._add_hints(instance=instances[0])` for custom as well as generated querysets. Under the existing router contract, an unset database resolves through the parent instance. The regression test uses `Room.objects.using("other").prefetch_related(Prefetch(relation, queryset=queryset))` and checks `[getattr(room, relation).name for room in rooms]` against `[f"{related_db} house 1", f"{related_db} house 2"]`, with `related_db = using or "other"`.

ReverseOneToOneDescriptor likewise adds `queryset._add_hints(instance=instances[0])` outside the default-queryset branch, enabling parent-instance routing for custom querysets. The database-selection regression covers the reverse relation through `for relation in ("house", "main_room_of")` and verifies database-specific related names and `getattr(room, relation)._state.db`.

The implementation only adds `queryset._add_hints(instance=instances[0])`; it does not assign a database or call `using()` on the custom queryset. Existing explicit-database precedence therefore remains intact. Regression coverage constructs `queryset = House.objects.using("default")`, reuses it across parent databases, and checks `self.assertEqual(house._state.db, "default")` and `self.assertEqual(queryset._db, "default")`.

Both descriptors add the instance hint before constructing relation filters: `queryset._add_hints(instance=instances[0])` precedes `rel_obj_attr = ...`. This updates hints without resolving or fixing a database. The existing hint-update and routing contracts preserve other hints and deferred routing. Tests supply `hints={"purpose": "prefetch"}` and assert `self.assertIs(hints.get("instance"), rooms[0])` and `self.assertEqual(hints["purpose"], "prefetch")`; explicit `using()` is covered by `read_router.db_for_read.assert_not_called()`.

The only runtime changes are the two `queryset._add_hints(instance=instances[0])` calls; existing batching, cache handling, cloning, and many-to-many paths remain unchanged. Reuse coverage checks `self.assertIsNone(queryset._db)` and `self.assertIsNone(queryset._result_cache)`. Cached-relation tests require `self.assertNumQueries(0, using="default")` and `self.assertNumQueries(0, using="other")`; partially cached coverage checks `self.assertIs(getattr(rooms[0], relation), cached_house)` with one related query. Empty coverage invokes `prefetch_related_objects([], Prefetch(relation, queryset=House.objects.all()))` and uses `House.objects.none()` under zero-query assertions.

verdicts.evidence: ForwardManyToOneDescriptor now executes `queryset = querysets[0]` followed by `queryset._add_hints(instance=instances[0])`. This supplies the parent instance to existing database routing, whose fallback uses the instance’s database when `_db` is unset. The added test checks distinct database contents with `["other house 1", "other house 2"]` and requires zero default-database queries.

ReverseOneToOneDescriptor likewise adds `queryset._add_hints(instance=instances[0])` immediately after selecting the custom queryset. The same established routing contract therefore applies to reverse one-to-one prefetches. The regression tests exercise both paths through `for lookup in ("house", "main_room_of")`.

The implementation adds only `queryset._add_hints(instance=instances[0])`; it does not assign `_db` or call `using()` to override the custom queryset. Existing explicit-database precedence remains intact. The regression test supplies `houses = House.objects.using(database)` and checks `self.assertEqual(houses._db, database)` and `router.db_for_read.assert_not_called()`.

`queryset._add_hints(instance=instances[0])` updates hints through the existing helper without resolving or fixing a database prematurely. Existing custom hints are preserved by that helper’s contract. The added test verifies `call.kwargs` equals `{"instance": rooms[0], "custom_hint": 42}` and checks `router.db_for_read.assert_not_called()` before evaluation.

Both implementation changes retain `queryset = querysets[0]` and merely add the instance hint; the existing noncustom branch remains `queryset = self.get_queryset(instance=instances[0])._disable_cloning()`. Existing filtering, cloning, cache handling, empty-input handling, and many-to-many paths remain unchanged. No per-object query loop is introduced. Added coverage checks reuse with `self.assertIsNone(houses._db)`, evaluated-cache preservation with `self.assertIs(houses._result_cache, original_cache)`, cached-relation identity, empty prefetch results, and bounded query counts.
